literal: Procedure for entering the Yin-Yang sequence: set communication dividend; remove conjunction cycle; when not full of conjunction number 358,888.5 it is new-moon entry into yang sequence parts; remove each in turn for new-moon entry into yin sequence parts; when each fills communication factor obtain one day; what does not fill is day remainder.
idiomatic: To enter the Yin-Yang sequence: take communication dividend, subtract conjunction cycle; remainder under conjunction number 358,888.5 is yang-sequence entry for the new moon; subtract each portion for yin entry; divide by communication factor for days; remainder is day remainder.

literal: Name the day, outside the count: the day entered in the sequence at midnight on the eleventh-month new moon.
idiomatic: Name the day (outside the count) for midnight sequence entry on month-11 new moon.

literal: To seek the next month:
idiomatic: To find the next month:

literal: Long month: add 2 days; short month: add 1 day; day remainder in each case 20,779.
idiomatic: Long month: add 2 days; short month: add 1 day; day remainder always 20,779.

literal: When the sequence fills 13 days and day remainder 15,987.5, then remove it.
idiomatic: When the sequence reaches 13 days with day remainder 15,987.5, drop that cycle.

literal: When yang ends, enter yin; when yin ends, enter yang.
idiomatic: At yang's end one enters yin; at yin's end one enters yang.

literal: To seek the next day: add one day.
idiomatic: For the next day: add one day.

literal: To seek new- and full-moon difference: multiply new-moon small remainder by 2,029; when full of 303 it makes day remainder; what does not fill, double it for small parts: that is new-moon difference number.
idiomatic: For new/full moon correction: multiply new-moon fractional remainder by 2,029; divide by 303 for day remainder; double the remainder for small parts to get new-moon difference.

literal: Add 14 days; day remainder 21,186; small parts 125.
idiomatic: Add 14 days, day remainder 21,186, and small parts 125.

literal: When small parts fill 606, carry to day remainder; when day remainder fills communication factor, it makes days: that is full-moon difference number.
idiomatic: When small parts reach 606, carry to day remainder; when day remainder fills communication factor, convert to days for full-moon difference.

literal: Add again for the next month's new moon.
idiomatic: Add again for the following new moon.

literal: To seek conjunction and lunar eclipse: set new- and full-moon midnight yin-yang sequence entry and remainder; when there is a half, remove it; set small parts 303; add the difference number.
idiomatic: For conjunction and eclipse: take midnight yin-yang sequence entry and remainder at new/full moon, drop halves, set small parts 303, and add the difference number.

literal: When small parts fill 606, carry to day remainder; when day remainder fills communication factor, carry to days; when days fill one sequence, remove it.
idiomatic: Carry small parts into day remainder and day remainder into days; when days complete one sequence, subtract the cycle.

literal: Name the day, outside the count: then the sequence entry at the hour of new or full moon.
idiomatic: Name the day (outside the count) for sequence entry at the instant of new or full moon.

literal: When new- or full-moon hour sequence entry is one day and day remainder 4,198 with small parts 428 or below, or twelve days with day remainder 11,788 and small parts 481 or above, at new moon there is conjunction; at full moon, lunar eclipse.
idiomatic: If hour-entry is 1 day with remainder ≤4,198 and small parts ≤428, or 12 days with remainder ≥11,788 and small parts ≥481, new moon yields conjunction and full moon yields eclipse.

literal: To seek the fixed greater and smaller remainders for conjunction and eclipse: let difference-number day remainder add to midnight slow-fast sequence remainder; when day remainder fills communication factor, carry to days: then sequence entry at the hour of new or full moon.
idiomatic: For fixed remainders at conjunction/eclipse: add difference day remainder to midnight slow-fast remainder; carry into days when remainder fills communication factor.

literal: Multiply sequence-entry remainder by decrease-increase rate; by decrease-increase adjust accumulated surplus-deficit parts; as difference factor to one; subtract surplus and add deficit from the original new/full small remainder for fixed small remainder.
idiomatic: Multiply sequence remainder by adjustment rate, adjust surplus-deficit parts, scale by difference factor, then subtract surplus or add deficit from base new/full fractional remainder.

literal: When increasing fills the factor or decreasing is insufficient, advance or retreat by the day factor.
idiomatic: On overflow or underflow in adjustment, carry or borrow using the day factor.

literal: To seek the hour of conjunction and eclipse: multiply fixed small remainder by 12; when full of day factor obtain one double-hour; name from zi, outside the count: the double-hour of the event.
idiomatic: For event hour: multiply fixed fractional remainder by 12, divide by day factor for double-hours; count from zi (outside the count).

literal: When there is remainder, quadruple it; when full of day factor obtain one as minor, two as half, three as major.
idiomatic: If remainder remains, multiply by four; each day-factor quotient gives minor (shao), half (ban), or major (tai) subdivisions.

literal: When there is still remainder, triple it; when full of day factor obtain one as strong; combine strong with minor for minor-strong, with half for half-strong, with major for major-strong.
idiomatic: Further remainder: multiply by three; quotients are strong (qiang); combine with prior subdivisions for compound labels.

literal: When two are obtained, that is minor-weak; combine with minor for half-weak, with half for major-weak, with major for one double-hour weak; name by the preceding double-hour.
idiomatic: Two quotients yield minor-weak; combine upward through half-weak and major-weak to a full weak double-hour named from the prior hour.

literal: To seek the moon's degrees from the solar path: set yin-yang sequence remainder, multiply by decrease-increase rate, as communication factor to one, by decrease-increase adjust the combined number for the fixed value.
idiomatic: For lunar latitude: take yin-yang sequence remainder, multiply by adjustment rate, divide by communication factor, and adjust the combined number.

literal: Fixed number: twelve to one makes degrees.
idiomatic: Divide the fixed number by twelve for degrees.

literal: What does not fill: four to one makes minor, half, and major.
idiomatic: The remainder in quarters yields minor, half, and major subdivisions.

literal: When still not filled, three to one: one is strong, two is minor-weak: that is the moon's degrees from the solar path.
idiomatic: Further remainder in thirds: one gives strong, two minor-weak, completing lunar distance from the ecliptic.

literal: Yang sequence is outside; yin sequence is inside.
idiomatic: Yang sequence is outside the path; yin sequence inside.

literal: Procedure for the five planets: set degree dividend; each remove its rate; from the remainder subtract the rate; the remainder, as era factor to one, is days entered in the year; what does not fill is day remainder; name from the civil new-year new moon, outside the count: day of planetary conjunction.
idiomatic: For each planet: take degree dividend, subtract its rate repeatedly; treat the remainder over era factor as days since civil new-year new moon (outside the count) for conjunction day.

literal: To seek the degree of conjunction: with days and remainder entered in the year, follow from civil new-year new-moon accumulated degrees and remainder; when remainder fills era factor, carry to degrees; when degrees fill 360, remove degree parts; name from Void I, outside the count: the degree where the planet conjoins.
idiomatic: For conjunction degree: add year-entry days and remainder to new-year solar accumulated degrees; carry at era factor; drop full circles; name from Void I (outside the count).

literal: To seek the day of planetary appearance: add the computed concealment days and remainder to conjunction day and remainder; when remainder fills era factor, carry to days; name as before: day of appearance.
idiomatic: For first visibility: add tabulated morning/evening concealment days and remainder to conjunction; carry remainder into days; name as before.

literal: To seek the degree of appearance: add computed concealment degrees and remainder to conjunction degree and remainder; when remainder fills era factor, carry to degrees; when entering Void, remove degree parts; name as before: degree of appearance.
idiomatic: For appearance degree: add concealment degrees and remainder to conjunction position; carry; subtract on entering Void; name as before.

literal: Procedure for planetary motion: divide degree remainder by small-part factor; the obtained is motion parts; what does not fill is small parts; daily add the motion parts; when full of factor, carry to degrees; when stationary, follow the prior; when retrograde, subtract; when concealed, do not exhaust degrees.
idiomatic: Planetary motion: convert degree remainder to motion and small parts; add daily motion; carry at factor; hold in station, subtract in retrograde; concealment may leave degrees unused.

literal: When direct motion enters Void, remove motion parts 6 and small parts 147; when retrograde emerges from Void, then add them.
idiomatic: On direct motion entering Void, subtract 6 motion parts and 147 small parts; add them when retrograde leaves Void.
